Farm view and Edit layout: one set of rules

A proposal, drawn over real Farm view screens. The same bar, panel and bottom edge in the Farm view and in Edit layout.
1. Where, and what
The bar says where you are. The panel shows what you opened. Neither holds the other's job.
2. The panel docks
Full height on the right, fixed width, its header fixed and its body scrolling. The bar and the buttons live in the map that is left, so nothing can overlap or stagger.
3. One stack, and it unwinds
Every page opens in the panel. The back chip names where you came from and puts the panel, the camera and the highlights back there. ✕, Esc or a click on empty map closes it all and returns to the place you started from.
4. One move
Opening something moves the camera once, straight to it, and keeps it in the free map, never under the panel.
5. Three spots on the bottom edge
View controls on the left; temporary bars in the middle (a selection, a placing guide); the mode button on the right: Select, or undo · redo · Done.
6. Edit is the same screen
At rest the bar holds Add and the place's actions and no panel shows. Adding goes to Plan and places first; the panel docks only for the details, or for the thing you pick.
House pattern. A docked inspector beside a canvas, as in maps and design tools; the panel keeps the Farm view's own look (tint, white cards, one header).
Attention budget. At rest: the place, three buttons, 3D and Select. Open: one panel. While placing: one guide. Never two things asking at once.
